evidence: $f2510 instruction 273 uniquely matches viewport division, camera scale, map radius and two origin-relative screen coordinates.
$f2510 reads map X/Y/radius with f32.load at 1509292/1509296/1509300. Radius times scale is passed to $f474, which emits canvas opcode 31; client.js opcode 31 calls arc.
$f2510 reads camera x/y/scale via f32.load offsets 8/12/16 and width/height via i32.load offsets 20/24.
Scale is f32(internalScale * max(f32(f32(height) / 1080), f32(f32(width) / 1920))). Origin screen coordinate is f32(viewport / 2 + f32(f32(origin - camera) * scale)).
$f2510 obtains the enclosing object by subtracting 185632 from the camera pointer.
$f997 allocates 258816 bytes, sets vtable 54080 at allocation + 185632, and stores allocation at its parameter + 536.
$f1387 and exported $ag call $f997 with 331784; therefore the allocation pointer is stored at 331784 + 536 = 332320. It must be reread at runtime; the camera base is not static.
$f1375 independently loads enclosing object from parent + 544, adds 185632 and reads/writes the camera fields. Parent singleton is 331776, agreeing with pointer address 332320.
$f1407/$f1409 create 64x64 terrain canvases. $f1375 emits draw rectangles at grid * 1024 - 1 with size 1026 through $f586; client.js opcode 35 calls drawImage with that rectangle.
These are static findings for this exact binary. Camera coordinates can be smoothed or spectating; identify them as camera/player coordinates until movement is visually validated.

$f2510 updates mapRadius 1509300 by smoothing toward f32(f32(object + 40) * 0.5 * f32(object + 396)), then uses that updated radius for the rendered circle. The value is dynamic, not a fixed map size. Map X/Y are smoothed renderer values as well.

$f996 decodes the target diameter/factor from received float32 data. $f1435 independently uses target center offsets 44/52 and the same target radius formula for distance-to-boundary calculations. The current mapRadius recipe tracks the rendered boundary and can lag the physical target while resizing.
